aboutH2: Jellinek Society: A Recovery House for Men in Edmonton
intro: The Jellinek Society runs Jellinek House, a 17-bed, abstinence-based home for men in early recovery from alcohol and drug addiction. It is meant for the stretch between treatment and living on your own, when a bit more time and structure help. Residents share the house with other men in recovery, go to 12 Step meetings, work with counselling staff and set goals such as going back to work or school or reconnecting with family. The society started in 1959 as the United Church Hostel and has run the house as the Jellinek Society since 1964.

pillars.title: Location in Edmonton
pillars.body: Jellinek Society is located in the Oliver neighborhood of Edmonton, Canada. This location is close to public transportation, making it easy to access the various resources in the city. The neighborhood is quiet and residential, providing a peaceful environment where men can focus on their recovery.

pillars.title: Community Engagement
pillars.body: Jellinek Society emphasizes community engagement as an important part of their recovery program. Residents are encouraged to participate in activities such as volunteer work, fitness classes, and hobbies. This helps men build a support network outside of the home and promotes a healthy, well-rounded lifestyle.

pillars.title: Outpatient Services
pillars.body: Jellinek Society offers outpatient services for individuals who have completed the residence program and want to continue their recovery journey. These services include ongoing counseling, peer support, and access to 12-Step meetings. Outpatient services also provide a way for Jellinek alumni to stay connected with the community and give back to those who are new to the program.

overview: The Jellinek Society is a rehab centre dedicated to treating individuals struggling with addiction to alcohol and other substances. Named after Dr. E.M. Jellinek, a pioneer in the field of alcoholism research, the society’s approach is rooted in the belief that addiction is a disease that can be effectively treated through a combination of medical and psychological interventions. Dr. Jellinek’s influential 1946 study, The Disease Concept of Alcoholism, continues to inform the Jellinek Society’s approach to addiction treatment, which emphasizes the physiological phases of alcoholism.

The Jellinek Society’s recovery house is housed in the former home of esteemed women’s rights activist, Nellie McClung and her family. Best known as a suffragist, author, and legislator, McClung was also a prohibitionist who advocated for the strict regulation of alcohol consumption and trade. Her passion for social justice and concern for the negative effects of alcoholism on individuals and families perfectly aligns with the Jellinek Society’s commitment to supporting individuals in their journey towards sobriety and wellness. The historic nature of the recovery house lends itself to a uniquely supportive and inspiring environment that promotes healing and recovery.

afterOverview: Life at Jellinek House is built around abstinence, confidentiality, dignity and respect, safety and structure, which the society names as its core values. There are no fees for service. Alongside the on-site 12 Step meetings, residents have one-on-one counselling, trauma-informed group sessions, a men's wisdom circle, a contemplative group, meditation and yoga every two weeks. The society recommends staying one to two years, which it says strengthens stability and sobriety. Any use of alcohol or drugs, or having paraphernalia in the house, ends a stay right away.

faqs.q: Who is eligible for the Jellinek Society program?
faqs.a: Men who are at least 18 years old and have been clean and sober for at least 30 days at the time of application are eligible. Having completed a residential treatment program within the last 3 years and being actively engaged in a 12-step fellowship (AA, NA, or CA) are encouraged. Candidates must also be either employed or actively seeking employment or educational training.

faqs.q: How much does the program cost?
faqs.a: There is no residency fee or deposit, and the society lists no fees for service.

faqs.q: How do I apply to Jellinek House?
faqs.a: Ask for an application by emailing support@jellinek.ca, by mail or in person at the house, then send it back the same way. A reference from an addiction counsellor, social worker or other professional is preferred, but self-referrals are considered. You may be asked to an in-person interview about your needs, goals and treatment plan.

Yes. Successful applicants go on a wait list, and how long it takes depends on when a bed opens. To stay on the list you need to call or visit Jellinek staff every Monday and Friday, so apply early and keep in touch.
The society recommends staying one to two years. Its recovery.com profile gives a range of 3 months to 2 years, with most residents staying 18 months to 2 years.

faqs.q: Does Jellinek Society offer detox or treatment?
faqs.a: No. Jellinek House is a supportive recovery residence, not a detox or medical treatment program. Applicants need at least 30 days clean and sober when they apply, and many come after finishing residential treatment elsewhere.

Yes, in large part. The society lists Recovery Alberta, Alberta Health Services, the United Church of Canada Foundation and Open Door Group among its main supporters, and its recovery.com profile says the program is fully funded through Recovery Alberta. That is why residents pay no residency fee.

Residents must stay abstinent from all intoxicants and avoid other addictive behaviours such as gambling. For everyone's safety, using alcohol or drugs, or having drug or alcohol paraphernalia, ends your residency right away.

faqs.q: Does Jellinek Society offer outpatient services?
faqs.a: Yes, Jellinek Society offers outpatient services for alumni who have completed the residence program.

faqs.q: Are family members allowed to visit?
faqs.a: Yes, family members are allowed to visit and participate in family therapy sessions.

faqs.q: What types of activities are available for residents?
faqs.a: Residents are encouraged to participate in volunteer work, fitness classes, and hobbies.

faqs.q: What kind of counseling is available?
faqs.a: Individual counseling and family therapy are available on-site.
